verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses:
notes: Here we have a short section (10:1-10) dealing with the regulations for blowing trumpets in times of war or in times of peace.

verses.zh: 「你要用银子做两枝号，都要锤出来的，用以招聚会众，并叫众营起行。
verses.en: “Make[NOTE:1] two trumpets of silver; you are to make[NOTE:2] them from a single hammered piece.[NOTE:3] You will use them[NOTE:4] for assembling the community and for directing the traveling of the camps.
notes: The Hebrew text uses what is called the “ethical dative”—“make [for] you two trumpets.” It need not be translated, but can simply be taken to underscore the direct imperative.
The imperfect tense is again instruction or legislation.

The instructions are not clearly spelled out here. But the trumpets were to be made of silver ingots beaten out into a sheet of silver and then bent to form a trumpet. There is archaeological evidence of silver smelting as early as 3000 b.c. Making silver trumpets would have been a fairly easy thing for the Israelites to do. The trumpet would have been straight, with a tapered form, very unlike the “ram’s horn” (שׁוֹפָר, shofar). The trumpets were used by the priests in Israel from the outset, but later were used more widely. The sound would be sharp and piercing, but limited in scope to a few notes. See further C. Sachs, The History of Musical Instruments.
Heb “and they shall be for you for assembling,” which is the way of expressing possession. Here the intent concerns how Moses was to use them.

verses.zh: 吹这号的时候，全会众要到你那里，聚集在会幕门口。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they blow[NOTE:2] them both, all the community must come[NOTE:3] to you to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
notes: The perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive is here subordinated as a temporal clause to the following similar verbal construction.
The verb תָקַע (taqaʿ) means “to strike, drive, blow a trumpet.”
Heb “the assembly shall assemble themselves.”

verses.zh: 若单吹一枝，众首领，就是以色列军中的统领，要聚集到你那里。
verses.en: “But if they blow with one trumpet, then the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, must come to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they shall assemble themselves.”

verses.zh: 吹出大声的时候，东边安的营都要起行。
verses.en: When you blow an alarm,[NOTE:1] then the camps that are located[NOTE:2] on the east side must begin to travel.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word for an alarm is תְּרוּעָה (teruʿah). The root verb of this word means “to give a blast on the trumpet.” It may also on occasion mean “give a shout” in battle (Josh 6:10). In this passage it must refer to the sound of the trumpet.
Heb “the camps that are camping.”
The perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive functions as the equivalent of the imperfect tense. Here the emphasis is on the start of the journey.

verses.zh: 二次吹出大声的时候，南边安的营都要起行。他们将起行，必吹出大声。
verses.en: And when you blow an alarm the second time, then the camps that are located on the south side must begin to travel.[NOTE:1] An alarm must be sounded[NOTE:2] for their journeys.
notes: The MT does not mention the departures of the northerly and westerly tribes. The Greek text completes the description by adding them, making a full schedule of the departure of the groups of tribes. The Greek is not likely to be original, however, since it carries all the signs of addition to complete the text, making a smooth, full reading. The MT is to be preferred; it apparently used two of the groups to give the idea.
The Hebrew text has “they shall blow an alarm”; the sentence without a formal subject should be taken as a passive idea.

verses.zh: 但招聚会众的时候，你们要吹号，却不要吹出大声。
verses.en: But when you assemble the community,[NOTE:1] you must blow the trumpets,[NOTE:2] but you must not sound an alarm.[NOTE:3]
notes: There is no expressed subject in the initial temporal clause. It simply says, “and in the assembling the assembly.” But since the next verb is the second person of the verb, that may be taken as the intended subject here.
Heb “blow”; the direct object (“trumpets”) has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
The signal for moving camp was apparently different in tone and may have been sharper notes or a different sequence. It was in some way distinguishable.

verses.zh: 亚伦子孙作祭司的要吹这号；这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。
verses.en: The sons of Aaron, the priests, must blow the trumpets, and they will be to you for an eternal ordinance throughout your generations.

verses.zh: 你们在自己的地，与欺压你们的敌人打仗，就要用号吹出大声，便在耶和华―你们的　神面前得蒙纪念，也蒙拯救脱离仇敌。
verses.en: If you go to war in your land against an adversary who opposes[NOTE:1] you, then you must sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the Lord your God, and you will be saved[NOTE:2] from your enemies.
notes: Both the “adversary” and “opposes” come from the same root: צָרַר (tsarar), “to hem in, oppress, harass,” or basically, “be an adversary.”
The Niphal perfect in this passage has the passive nuance and not a reflexive idea—the Israelites would be spared because God remembered them.

verses.zh: 在你们快乐的日子和节期，并月朔，献燔祭和平安祭，也要吹号，这都要在你们的　神面前作为纪念。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: “Also, in the time when you rejoice, such as[NOTE:1] on your appointed festivals or[NOTE:2] at the beginnings of your months, you must blow with your trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings, so that they may[NOTE:3] become[NOTE:4] a memorial for you before your God: I am the Lord your God.”
notes: The conjunction may be taken as explicative or epexegetical, and so rendered “namely; even; that is,” or it may be taken as emphatic conjunction, and translated “especially.”
The vav (ו) is taken here in its alternative use and translated “or.”
The form is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive. After the instruction imperfects, this form could be given the same nuance, or more likely, subordinated as a purpose or result clause.
The verb הָיָה (hayah, “to be”) has the meaning “to become” when followed by the preposition ל (lamed).

verses.zh: 第二年二月二十日，云彩从法柜的帐幕收上去。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] On the twentieth day of the second month, in the second year, the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle of the testimony.[NOTE:2]
notes: This section is somewhat mechanical: It begins with an introduction (vv. 11, 12), and then begins with Judah (vv. 13-17), followed by the rest of the tribes (vv. 18-27), and finally closes with a summary (v. 28). The last few verses (vv. 29-36) treat the departure of Hobab.

The expression is difficult; it is מִשְׁכַּן הָעֵדֻת (mishkan haʿedut). The reference is to the sacred shrine that covered the ark with the commandments inside. NEB renders the expression as “tabernacle of the Token”; NAB has “the dwelling of the commandments.”tc Smr inserts a lengthy portion from Deut 1:6-8, expressing the command for Israel to take the land from the Amorites.

verses.zh: 以色列人就按站往前行，离开西奈的旷野，云彩停住在巴兰的旷野。
verses.en: So the Israelites set out[NOTE:1] on their journeys from the desert[NOTE:2] of Sinai; and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
notes: The verb is the same as the noun: “they journeyed on their journeyings.” This underscores the point of their continual traveling.

The Hebrew term מִדְבָּר (midbar) refers to a dry region which may be characterized as receiving less than twelve inches of rain per year. It therefore cannot support trees but may have sparse vegetation if it receives at least six inches of rain. At less than six inches of rain the term “desert” is certainly appropriate, though this would not mean a sandy desert. The Sinai peninsula includes both treeless “wilderness” and “desert.” While there is some dispute about the location of Mt. Sinai, NET has chosen “desert of Sinai” as the designation for the region around Mt. Sinai. The same Hebrew term is used later in the verse in connection with Paran, but rendered as the “wilderness of Paran.”

verses.zh: 这是他们照耶和华藉摩西所吩咐的，初次往前行。
verses.en: This was the first time they set out on their journey according to the commandment[NOTE:1] of the Lord, by the authority[NOTE:2] of Moses.
notes: Heb “mouth.”
Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 按着军队首先往前行的是犹大营的纛。统领军队的是亚米拿达的儿子拿顺。
verses.en: The standard[NOTE:1] of the camp of the Judahites set out first according to their companies, and over his company was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
notes: The “standard” (דֶּגֶל, degel) was apparently some kind of a symbol put up on a pole to signify the tribal hosts. R. de Vaux thought it simply referred to a pole or a mast, but that would not distinguish tribes (Ancient Israel, 226-27).

verses.zh: 统领以萨迦支派军队的是苏押的儿子拿坦业。
verses.en: Over the company of the tribe of Issacharites was Nathanel son of Zuar,

verses.zh: 统领西布伦支派军队的是希伦的儿子以利押。
verses.en: and over the company of the tribe of the Zebulunites was Eliab son of Helon.

verses.zh: 帐幕拆卸，革顺的子孙和米拉利的子孙就抬着帐幕先往前行。
verses.en: Then the tabernacle was dismantled, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.

verses.zh: 按着军队往前行的是流便营的纛。统领军队的是示丢珥的儿子以利蓿。
verses.en: The standard of the camp of Reuben set out according to their companies; over his company was Elizur son of Shedeur.

verses.zh: 统领西缅支派军队的是苏利沙代的儿子示路蔑。
verses.en: Over the company of the tribe of the Simeonites was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,

verses.zh: 统领迦得支派军队的是丢珥的儿子以利雅萨。
verses.en: and over the company of the tribe of the Gadites was Eliasaph son of Deuel.

verses.zh: 哥辖人抬着圣物先往前行。他们未到以前，抬帐幕的已经把帐幕支好。
verses.en: And the Kohathites set out, carrying the articles for the sanctuary;[NOTE:1] the tabernacle was to be set up[NOTE:2] before they arrived.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “carrying the sanctuary,” a metonymy of whole for parts, representing all the holy objects that were located in the sanctuary.
The verb is the third person plural form; without an expressed subject it is treated as a passive.
Heb “against their coming.”

verses.zh: 按着军队往前行的是以法莲营的纛，统领军队的是亚米忽的儿子以利沙玛。
verses.en: And the standard of the camp of the Ephraimites set out according to their companies; over his company was Elishama son of Ammihud.

verses.zh: 统领玛拿西支派军队的是比大蓿的儿子迦玛列。
verses.en: Over the company of the tribe of the Manassehites was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

verses.zh: 统领便雅悯支派军队的是基多尼的儿子亚比但。
verses.en: and over the company of the tribe of Benjaminites was Abidan son of Gideoni.

verses.zh: 在诸营末后的是但营的纛，按着军队往前行。统领军队的是亚米沙代的儿子亚希以谢。
verses.en: The standard of the camp of the Danites set out, which was the rear guard[NOTE:1] of all the camps by their companies; over his company was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
notes: The MT uses a word that actually means “assembler,” so these three tribes made up a strong rear force recognized as the assembler of all the tribes.

verses.zh: 统领亚设支派军队的是俄兰的儿子帕结。
verses.en: Over the company of the tribe of the Asherites was Pagiel son of Ocran,

verses.zh: 统领拿弗他利支派军队的是以南的儿子亚希拉。
verses.en: and over the company of the tribe of the Naphtalites was Ahira son of Enan.

verses.zh: 以色列人按着军队往前行，就是这样。
verses.en: These were the traveling arrangements[NOTE:1] of the Israelites according to their companies when they traveled.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “journeyings of.”
The verb is the preterite with vav (ו) consecutive. But in this sentence it should be subordinated as a temporal clause to the preceding statement, even though it follows it.

verses.zh: 摩西对他岳父（或译：内兄）―米甸人流珥的儿子何巴―说：「我们要行路，往耶和华所应许之地去；他曾说：『我要将这地赐给你们。』现在求你和我们同去，我们必厚待你，因为耶和华指着以色列人已经应许给好处。」
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel, the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law,[NOTE:2] “We are journeying to the place about which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will treat you well,[NOTE:3] for the Lord has promised good things[NOTE:4] for Israel.”
notes: For additional bibliography for this short section, see W. F. Albright, “Jethro, Hobab, and Reuel in Early Hebrew Tradition,” CBQ 25 (1963): 1-11; G. W. Coats, “Moses in Midian,” JBL 92 (1973): 3-10; B. Mazar, “The Sanctuary of Arad and the Family of Hobab the Kenite,” JNES 24 (1965): 297-303; and T. C. Mitchell, “The Meaning of the Noun ḥtn in the Old Testament,” VT 19 (1969): 93-112.

There is a problem with the identity of Hobab. The MT says that he is the son of Reuel, making him the brother-in-law of Moses. But Judg 4:11 says he is the father-in-law. In Judg 1:16; 4:11 Hobab is traced to the Kenites, but in Exod 3:1 and 18:1 Jethro (Reuel) is priest of Midian. Jethro is identified with Reuel on the basis of Exod 2:18 and 3:1, and so Hobab becomes Moses’ חֹתֵן (khoten), a relative by marriage and perhaps brother-in-law. There is not enough information to decide on the identity and relationships involved here. Some suggest that there is one person with the three names (G. B. Gray, Numbers [ICC], 93); others suggest Hobab is a family name (R. F. Johnson, IDB 2:615), and some suggest that the expression “the son of Reuel the Midianite” had dropped out of the genealogy of Judges, leading to the conflict (J. Crichton, ISBE 2:1055). If Hobab is the same as Jethro, then Exod 18:27 does not make much sense, for Jethro did go home. On this basis many conclude Hobab is a brother-in-law. This would mean that after Jethro returned home, Moses conversed with Hobab, his brother-in-law. For more discussion, see the articles and the commentaries.

The verb is the Hiphil of the root “to be good” (יָטַב, yatav); it may be translated “treat well, deal favorably, generously with.” Here it is a perfect tense with vav (ו) following the imperative, showing a sequence in the verbal ideas.
The Hebrew text simply has “has spoken good” for Israel.

verses.zh: 何巴回答说：「我不去；我要回本地本族那里去。」
verses.en: But Hobab[NOTE:1] said to him, “I will not go, but I will go instead to my own land and to my kindred.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Hobab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 摩西说：「求你不要离开我们；因为你知道我们要在旷野安营，你可以当作我们的眼目。
verses.en: Moses[NOTE:1] said, “Do not leave us,[NOTE:2] because you know places for us to camp in the wilderness, and you could be our guide.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Moses) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The form with אַל־נָא (ʾal naʾ) is a jussive; negated it stresses a more immediate request, as if Hobab is starting to leave, or at least determined to leave.

In the Hebrew text the expression is more graphic: “you will be for us for eyes.” Hobab was familiar with the entire Sinai region, and he could certainly direct the people where they were to go. The text does not record Hobab’s response. But the fact that Kenites were in Canaan as allies of Judah (Judg 1:16) would indicate that he gave in and came with Moses. The first refusal may simply be the polite Semitic practice of declining first so that the appeal might be made more urgently.

verses.zh: 你若和我们同去，将来耶和华有甚么好处待我们，我们也必以甚么好处待你。」
verses.en: And if you come with us, it is certain[NOTE:1] that whatever good things the Lord will favor us with, we will share with you as well.”
notes: Heb “and it shall be.”

verses.zh: 以色列人离开耶和华的山，往前行了三天的路程；耶和华的约柜在前头行了三天的路程，为他们寻找安歇的地方。
verses.en: So they traveled from the mountain of the Lord three days’ journey;[NOTE:1] and the ark of the covenant of the Lord was traveling before them during the three days’ journey, to find a resting place for them.
notes: The phrase “a journey of three days” is made up of the adverbial accusative qualified with the genitives.

verses.zh: 他们拔营往前行，日间有耶和华的云彩在他们以上。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] And the cloud of the Lord was over them by day, when they traveled[NOTE:2] from the camp.
notes: The scribes sensed that there was a dislocation with vv. 34-36, and so they used the inverted letters nun (נ) as brackets to indicate this.
The adverbial clause of time is composed of the infinitive construct with a temporal preposition and a suffixed subjective genitive.

verses.zh: 约柜往前行的时候，摩西就说：「耶和华啊，求你兴起！愿你的仇敌四散！愿恨你的人从你面前逃跑！」
verses.en: And when the ark traveled, Moses would say, “Rise up, O Lord! May your enemies be scattered, and may those who hate you flee before you!”

verses.zh: 约柜停住的时候，他就说：「耶和华啊，求你回到以色列的千万人中！」
verses.en: And when it came to rest he would say, “Return, O Lord, to the many thousands of Israel!”[NOTE:1]
notes: These two formulaic prayers were offered by Moses at the beginning and at the end of the journeys. They prayed for the Lord to fight ahead of the nation when it was on the move, and to protect them when they camped. The theme of the first is found in Ps 68:1. The prayers reflect the true mentality of holy war, that it was the Lord who fought for Israel and defended her. The prayers have been included in the prayer book for synagogue services.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 10:1-10

1The Lord spoke further to Moses, saying, 2"Make yourself two
trumpets of silver, of hammered work you shall make them; and you shall use them for summoning the congregation and
for having the camps set out. 3When both are blown, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the
doorway of the tent of meeting. 4Yet if only one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the divisions
of Israel, shall assemble before you. 5But when you blow an alarm, the camps that are pitched on the east
side shall set out. 6When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that are pitched on the south side
shall set out; an alarm is to be blown for them to set out. 7When convening the assembly, however, you shall
blow without sounding an alarm. 8The priestly sons of Aaron, moreover, shall blow the trumpets; and this shall
be for you a perpetual statute throughout your generations. 9When you go to war in your land against the
adversary who attacks you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, that you may be remembered before the
Lord your God, and be saved from your enemies. 10Also in the day of your
gladness and in your appointed feasts, and on the first days of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your
burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be as a reminder of you before your God.
I am the Lord your God."

10:2 "two trumpets of silver" We find the same kind of trumpets in Egypt. This proves the historicity of this account.
The marching order of the Hebrew tribes, the wheeled ox-carts, the silver trumpets, and the shaving of the entire bodies of the
priests are all elements of Egyptian culture (see Intro. to Numbers). From Josephus' Antiquities of the Jews 3.12.6; and from
Arch of Titus we learn that these silver trumpets were straight in shape with a flared end and were about eighteen inches long.

These trumpets had several functions.

- When both were blown together it signaled Israel to meet at the tent of meeting, Num. 10:2,3.

- When only one was blown, the leaders gathered at the tent of meeting, Num. 10:4.

- When they were blown the whole camp was to move out, Num. 10:2,5-6.

- When they are blown it was time to prepare for battle, Num. 10:7,9.

- They were blown at the beginning of feast days, Num. 10:10.

Remember that the camp of Israel was designed in the same way as Rameses II's army, so Israel was
organized as an army and marched as an army.

There is Jewish tradition (Mishnah) that the silver trumpets were blown, not only one or two of them,
but with different sounds.

- a long blast

- three different notes

See SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED
BY ISRAEL. Josephus described the silver trumpets in Antiq. 3.12.6.

"blow an alarm"

This Hebrew term (BDB 929) can mean

- a shout

- a war cry (cf. Num. 10:9; 31:6; Josh. 6:5,20)

- a shout for joy

The exact differentiation between the signals the trumpets gave is uncertain (JPSOA footnote).

10:6 The MT does not list all the tribes but the LXX does.

10:8 "a perpetual statute" Notice its usage in Exod. 12:14,17; Lev. 3:17; 7:36. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam) and
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S
REVELATION.

10:9 "be saved from your enemies" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT).

10:10 "I am the Lord your God" This is covenant language. For "Lord" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
For "God" see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR
DEITY, C.

There is no VERB in this phrase, just the FIRST PERSON PRONOUN and
two NOUNS (BDB 43 and 217).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 10:11-16

11Now in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud was lifted from over the
tabernacle of the testimony; 12and the sons of Israel set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai. Then
the cloud settled down in the wilderness of Paran. 13So they moved out for the first time according to the
commandment of the Lord through Moses. 14The standard of the camp of the sons
of Judah, according to their armies, set out first, with Nahshon the son of Amminadab, over its army, 15and Nethanel
the son of Zuar, over the tribal army of the sons of Issachar; 16and Eliab the son of Helon over the tribal army of the
sons of Zebulun.

10:11-21:35 A new literary unit which covers 38 years begins here.

- Israel leaves Mt. Sinai and moves to Kadesh, Num. 10:11-12:16

- Israel at Kadesh, Num. 13:1-20:13

- Israel leaves Kadesh for the plains of Moab, Num. 20:14-21:35

10:11 "the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month" This is a very specific date. This would
be nineteen days after the census of Num. 1:1.

The specificity is evidence of the historicity of the account. See Special Topics:

10:25 "the rear guard" The tribe of Dan was the last. It formed a military unit known as "the rear guard."
While Israel traveled through the wildernesses she had to always be on guard for attack. Her camp and
marching order were designed after Rameses II's army camp. Moses was trained in Egypt's military schools.

In later passages this descriptive title is used for Mt. Zion, which is a collective term for Jerusalem and

▣ "the ark of the covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE
COVENANT and SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

The ark was normally in the Holy of Holies within the inner shrine, but when Israel traveled it was
taken to the front! YHWH went before His people in guidance and protection.

▣ "a resting place" Here, this (BDB 629) refers to a proper camping site (TEV, NJB). This term also has
the connotation of peace, security, and rest because of YHWH's presence with His people.

The term is used of the "Promised Land" (i.e., Canaan) in Deut. 12:9; Ps. 95:11. In Isaiah 32:18 it has
an eschatological connotation.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- List the items that show Israel's historical links to Egypt.

- In how many ways were the silver trumpets used?

- Why do scholars assert a contextual break at Num. 10:11?

- Why does Moses want Hobab to come with him?

- Was the ark in the midst of the camp or at the front?

- Why does Moses pray YHWH will return in Num. 10:36?
